attractions.name: Hiran Minar
attractions.description: A Mughal-era monument and reservoir built by Emperor Jahangir in memory of his pet antelope, a unique and peaceful historic site.

attractions.name: Sheikhupura Fort
attractions.description: A Mughal-era fort built by Emperor Jahangir, later used by Sikh rulers, showcasing a blend of architectural styles.

attractions.name: Nankana Sahib (day trip)
attractions.description: The birthplace of Guru Nanak, founder of Sikhism, and one of the most sacred Sikh pilgrimage sites in the world, a short trip from Sheikhupura.

food_places.name: GT Road highway restaurants
food_places.specialty: Popular stopover restaurants for travelers on GT Road

transportation.notes: Rickshaws are common for short trips

weather_info.climate_type: Semi-arid, continental climate with hot summers and cool winters

travel_tips.tip: Sheikhupura sits directly on GT Road/the M-2 corridor, making it an easy stopover between Lahore and Faisalabad.
Combine a visit to Hiran Minar, Sheikhupura Fort, and Nankana Sahib into a single day trip from Lahore if time is limited.
Standard travel precautions apply; the area is generally calm and welcoming to visitors, including Sikh pilgrims visiting Nankana Sahib.
Visit Hiran Minar in the early morning or late afternoon for the best light over the reservoir.

history.founded: Founded in the early 17th century by Mughal Emperor Jahangir
history.city_history: Sheikhupura was established by Emperor Jahangir as a hunting ground, giving rise to landmarks like Hiran Minar and Sheikhupura Fort. The nearby town of Nankana Sahib, within Sheikhupura district, is one of the holiest sites in Sikhism as the birthplace of Guru Nanak.
history.province_history: Punjab, meaning 'land of five rivers', has one of the longest continuous histories in South Asia, home to the ancient Indus Valley Civilization (Harappa), later ruled by the Mauryas, Mughals, Sikh Empire, and the British before becoming part of Pakistan in 1947.
